summary: Modern databases increasingly embed AI/ML directly into the data layer, letting teams run inference, generate embeddings, and perform semantic (vector) search using SQL without moving data to external services. The vector database market is growing rapidly (projected to reach ~USD 17.91 billion by 2034 at ~24% CAGR), with pgvector, native vector indexes, and managed LLM integrations (e.g., Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML + Vertex AI, Databricks Mosaic AI) becoming standard features. Capabilities range from fully native vector search to extension-based support, so precise distinctions matter when choosing a platform.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, ML functions)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex runs managed AI models inside Snowflake, callable as SQL functions (e.g., COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EMBED_TEXT), so data never leaves the platform and no external LLM provider or self-managed GPUs are required. It also includes Cortex Search for retrieval and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and the managed Cortex Search service for hybrid semantic retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in hosted LLMs (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, Anthropic Claude) accessed via Cortex SQL/REST functions; no external API calls needed.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits, billed by tokens processed per Cortex function and compute used; charged on top of standard warehouse/storage costs.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (SQL-based model training) with Vertex AI integration for generative AI
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using standard SQL, and integrates with Vertex AI to call foundation models (Gemini) for text generation, embeddings, and remote inference directly from queries via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF) and the ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING function for generating embeddings in-database.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI foundation models (Gemini, text embeddings, PaLM-era models) accessed through remote models and SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery on-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based slots; generative AI/embedding calls incur Vertex AI model usage charges in addition to BigQuery compute.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: Open-source extensions: pgvector for embeddings/similarity search and pgai/pgvectorscale for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: With pgvector (and optionally Apache AGE for graph queries), embeddings, retrieval, and relationships all live in the same database as the rest of the application data. The pgai extension adds functions to generate embeddings and call LLMs directly from SQL, enabling RAG pipelines within Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Via extension (but considered native to self-managed PostgreSQL). pgvector adds the vector type with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; it is an extension rather than a core-engine feature, though it is the de facto standard for Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: pgai enables calling external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere, Anthropic, etc.) from SQL; otherwise integrates via application frameworks like LangChain.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free to use; cost is driven by the hosting/compute infrastructure plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models from SQL queries by calling out to Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend, adding predictions, sentiment analysis, and generative AI responses to query results without building custom integration code.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided only through the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML feature; the ML service does not include a native vector index.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models via SQL functions (e.g., aws_ml, aws_bedrock functions).
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend inference charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL with SageMaker/Bedrock integration
databases.description: Redshift ML lets data warehouse users create, train, and deploy ML models using standard SQL (CREATE MODEL), automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot under the hood, and run predictions directly in queries. It also supports calling Amazon Bedrock LLMs for generative AI from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native within Redshift ML. Redshift does not provide a built-in vector search index as part of the ML service; vector/semantic search typically relies on external services or embeddings stored and compared manually.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker for custom/foundation models and Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference via SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML uses existing Redshift compute; training leverages SageMaker (billed separately), and inference runs in-cluster or via remote model endpoints with associated charges.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, foundation model APIs) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform via Mosaic AI for building, fine-tuning, and serving models, along with Foundation Model APIs for LLM access and governance through Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search delivers managed, serverless semantic retrieval integrated with the lakehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector database that automatically syncs embeddings from Delta tables and supports approximate nearest-neighbor search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving provide access to hosted and third-party LLMs (Llama, DBRX, external providers) with fine-tuning and RAG tooling.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and vector search endpoints, plus underlying cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector indexing and semantic search within the document database
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings alongside operational document data and performs approximate nearest-neighbor semantic search using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, enabling RAG and recommendation use cases without a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is built into Atlas via dedicated vector indexes (HNSW) and the $vectorSearch operator, supporting hybrid search combined with normal document filters.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, Cohere, etc.) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex to generate and query embeddings.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or cluster resources billed as part of Atlas consumption/instance pricing.
